newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer amid supply uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer amid supply uncertainties.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher Friday, adding to a week of heady gains, but dealings in the last session of the week were subdued as the market appeared to consolidate, traders said.
The May contract settled 0.35 cent firmer at 112.70 cents per lb, up 5.90 cents on the week.
Most-active July went out 1.05 cents higher at 110.95 cents, with spot April ending 0.75 cent firmer at 114.70 cents. Volume was estimated at 15,000 lots.
"Ultimately I think the gains will be held," John Gross of the Copper Journal said. "Inventories are low relative to where the price is, demand is quite good and there is labor uncertainty."
LME stocks fell 1,550 tonnes Friday to 145,200 tonnes.

Total LME and COMEX stocks are now down to 211,306 short tons compared to 238,951 tons at the end of March, though in the U.S., combined LME and COMEX stocks have risen to 100,333 tons from 74,844 tons at the end of December.
The strike at Escondida mine in Chile continues, while labor talks at Phelps Dodge's Chino mine in New Mexico have failed to reach agreement on a new labor deal so far.

At Chile's Quebrada Blanca mine on Sunday workers will vote on whether to accept the company's final pay offer. Workers at Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting in Canada have been working without a labor contract for weeks.
Kennecott Utah Copper's blister smelter is also in the middle of a maintenance shutdown.
Gross said historically spot copper prices should be around 120 to 125 cents per pound at current inventory levels.

The cash to three months backwardation on LME flared during the week end at $200/$210 to provide the main upward price thrust, and traders said further surges could come next week when the very tight LME nearby prompts are due from Monday, traders said.
